targets.title: Approach-motivated positive affect reduces breadth of attention.
targets.evidence_quote: Here, therefore, we conducted a registered conceptual replication where we assessed whether the narrowing of attentional breadth following dessert (vs rocks) pictures replicated with a new picture set.
targets.outcome_quote: Participants rated the desserts as more positive in valence and higher in motivational intensity than the rocks. However, attentional breadth was invariant across image type and perceptual focality, and across participant ratings of valence and motivational intensity. These findings challenge the robustness with which emotion and motivation influence attentional breadth.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract states the original dessert-versus-rock narrowing and reports invariant attentional breadth in the conceptual replication, directly challenging the central finding.
